newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian minister blames West for Lagos bombings.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian minister blames West for Lagos bombings.

text.p: Nigeria's information minister accused unnamed Western nations on Thursday of being behind a spate of bombings in Lagos with the intention of putting pressure on the military government.

"Because we are not yielding to their pressure, Western nations are now going about sponsoring people to plant bombs to cause trouble and destabilise our country," Walter Ofonagoro told a news conference in the capital Abuja.
He did not name any particular nation.
On Tuesday the latest in a series of bomb blasts in Lagos since December ripped apart an army bus, killing two soldiers and wounding nearly 30.
Nigeria has blamed the exiled opposition for the attacks.
"The Western world is trying to dictate to us our destiny," Ofonagoro said. "We will not allow this...the terrorists will fail and will soon be unmasked," he added.
"They are trying to push the government to declare a state of emergency but the government won't," he said.
Nigeria plunged into political crisis in 1993 when the military annulled a presidential election to restore democracy.

Relations with the West worsened further in 1995 when General Sani Abacha's government defied international opinion and hanged nine minority rights activists, including writer Ken Saro-Wiwa, over the murder of four chiefs.

The European Union and the United States have called for greater respect for human rights by Nigerian rulers and a quicker return to democracy than the October 1998 date set by Abacha to hand over to an elected president.

But the government says it will go ahead with its programme and on Thursday the electoral commission announced that municipal polls would be held on March 15 before state elections later this year and federal polls in 1998.
